title: Render Depth Of Field | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive
description:

markdown_content: ## Introduction to Depth of Field in Clo 2025.0 This section introduces the new depth of field feature in Clo 2025.0, explaining its relevance and basic camera concepts. Depth of field (DoF) refers to the focusing and zooming effects in rendering that influence how sharp or blurry objects appear at different distances. ## Accessing the Render Window and Camera Settings To use depth of field in Clo, open the render window via the top toolbar by selecting **Render > Render**. The render window includes rendering tools, an object browser, and a property editor. Selecting the camera icon within the render toolbar reveals camera-specific options in the property editor. Enabling **Physical Camera Render Only** activates advanced camera controls, including depth of field settings, exposure, and other physical camera parameters. ## Understanding Depth of Field and Custom Views Depth of field affects sharpness based on the camera focus and zoom. In Clo, users often create **custom views**—saved camera angles of a project accessed by right-clicking in the 3D window (outside avatars or garments). Different objects in these views may appear differently blurred due to depth of field averaging and zoom differences between views. Previously, depth of field settings applied globally, making it difficult to control sharpness per custom view. Clo 2025.0 introduces the ability to **tie depth of field settings to individual custom views**, enabling more precise control over focus and blur per angle. ## Configuring Depth of Field per Custom View 1. Select a custom view and enable **Interactive** mode for easier adjustment. 2. In the camera settings, check **Physical Camera Render Only** and turn on **Depth of Field**. 3. Under **Viewpoint Focus**, switch from **Current View** to **Custom Views**. 4. Use the **Focus by Left Click** option to click directly on the 3D window where you want the focus point to be. This sets the camera's focus distance automatically for that custom view. 5. Repeat for each custom view, clicking on different focus points as needed. The focus updates dynamically and is saved per custom view. This method allows users to avoid guessing numeric focus values, making focus adjustments intuitive even for those less familiar with camera settings. ## Rendering with Depth of Field and Custom Views Once depth of field is configured for all desired custom views: - Go to **Image Settings** and set the render target to **Custom Views**. - Adjust any additional rendering parameters as needed. - Render the scene once, and Clo will apply the correct depth of field settings per each custom view automatically. The output images will show varying sharpness and blur effects depending on the selected focus points, demonstrating how depth of field enhances realism and visual storytelling in renders. ## Summary and Use Cases The updated depth of field feature in Clo 2025.0 enables: - Per-custom-view depth of field control. - Intuitive focus setting by clicking directly on objects. - Reduced need for multiple separate renders. - Improved realism and flexibility in presenting multiple angles with different focuses in one render session. This feature is ideal for users who understand camera mechanics and want precise control over their renders’ focus and blur effects to enhance visual communication. --- This completes the detailed guide on using the new Render Depth of Field feature in Clo 2025.0.
